Top tips - Choose Reserved seats if you don't want to stand - Recommended for popular routes like Tokyo to Kyoto and at popular times of year ## How to book and use Japan train tickets with Trip.com ![Search for trains](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1ny2t12000tkrwlqgEABB.png) ### Step 01 ### Search for trains Enter your origin and destination, select your travel dates and number of passengers. Add a return date if needed to see Shinkansen schedules on Trip.com. ![Select your departure and seat class](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1ny2b12000tkrwilt5E14.png) ### Step 02 ### Select your departure and seat class Pick your departure time and choose Ordinary or Green Car class. Click through and complete the passenger details in the form. ![Pay securely](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1ny1r12000tkrx4929332.png) ### Step 03 ### Pay securely Complete your booking and pay in your chosen currency with secure payment methods, including credit/debit cards, Apple Pay, PayPal, and Google Pay. ![Receive your QR code](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1ny1f12000tkrwilsF8FD.png) ### Step 04 ### Receive your QR code Receive your e-tickets and itinerary details via email or through the Trip.com app. Confirmation is instant as soon as payment is complete. ![Enter the station](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1ny1712000smhd5cs2ECD.png) ### Step 05 ### Enter the station For most journeys, you can go through the ticket gates by scanning your QR code. If needed, you can easily print tickets at the ticket machine. ![Board the train](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1ny1512000smhdb2yDF39.png) ### Step 06 ### Board the train Scan your QR code or insert your paper ticket into the barriers to access the platforms and board the train. ## Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen baggage allowance Shinkansen luggage policies can vary slightly by line, but baggage allowance is uniform across all Shinkansen routes. If you're traveling with oversized luggage, you'll need to review the Shinkansen luggage rules a bit more closely. ![Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen baggage allowance](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1ny3u12000t2aklcvEC07.jpg_.webp) ### Standard luggage allowance - Passengers may bring up to **2 pieces of luggage** for no additional fee (not including personal items like handbags, umbrellas). - Each item must weigh **30 kg** or less. - Total luggage **dimensions must not exceed 250 cm.** - Bags with total dimensions up to 160 cm can be placed in at your feet, in the overhead racks or in the dedicated luggage area. ### Oversized baggage Baggage with total **dimensions between 161 cm and 250 cm** (height + width + depth) are considered oversized baggage. Passengers with oversized baggage must **reserve an oversized baggage seat** on lines between some major cities (same price as regular reserved seat). These seats are usually found at the last row of each car, and oversized bags can be placed in the space behind your seat. Traveling without a reservation for this luggage space can result in a fine on some lines. ### Shinkansen luggage tips - If you need oversized baggage space, make sure you **book your seat** early, as they are limited in number and often sell out during busy seasons. - **Green Class** (i.e. First Class) cars usually include extra space for luggage, which is particularly helpful in peak months like May, August and December to early January. - **Bicycles must be folded** or disassembled and stored in a bike bag. - Luggage forwarding services - such as Luggage Express - can **have your luggage delivered** from your departure hotel to your arrival hotel so you can travel light. ## Shinkansen child tickets from Tokyo to Nagano There are three categories of Shinkansen child tickets, each with different pricing and age limits. Consult the different ticket categories below. | Category | Age Group | Fare Price | Tokyo to Nagano | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Adult ticket | 12+ years old | 100% (Full Price) | $51.84 | | Child | 6 – 11 years old | 50% (Half Price) | $25.92 | | Infant | 1 – 5 years old | Free | 0 | | Baby | Under 1 year old | Free | 0 | ### When you need to buy a child ticket for anB55 infant Infants (1 to 5 years) and babies (under 1 year) generally travel free on Shinkansen trains, except in some specific situations as follows: - **When they need their own seat:** If your infant is occupying their own reserved seat - rather than sitting on your lap - then you must buy them a Child Ticket. - **When you're traveling with three infants:** One fare-paying passenger can be accompanied by up to two infants for free. For three or more accompanying infants, a Child fare is required for the third and subsequent infants. - **When traveling alone:** Infants traveling unaccompanied (rare for tourists, but a rule nonetheless) requires a Child ticket. ### Reserved seat prices for children: Ordinary, Green Car and Gran Class If your kid needs their own reserved seat, a charge will apply for their seat. This will vary depending on the car class: - **Ordinary Car:** A 50% charge of the total fare applies for Children's reserved seats (ages 6-11). - **Green Car & Gran Class:** The Luxury Surcharge for Green and Gran Class does not have a child discount. You must pay the full adult rate for children's seats. ## Refunds and changes for Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen tickets The Shinkansen refund and change policy allows for some flexibility when it comes to your Shinkansen ticket, but some charges may apply depending on your ticket type. ### Changing your Shinkansen booking - Standard fare Shinkansen tickets allow a **one-time change free of charge** for the same type of ticket for unused tickets. If you change to a ticket of greater value, you must pay the difference. If you change to a ticket of lesser value, you will be refunded the difference. - However, specific Shinkansen modification policies **vary by ticket type**: deep discount and advance fares usually do not permit changes, or if they do, they may not provide refunds in fare difference. As such, always check the conditions of your specific ticket type. ### Refund fees - Any unused, valid Shinkansen ticket can be refunded, but will be subject to a **cancellation charge** according to ticket type. You must apply for a refund before the train departs, otherwise you cannot be refunded. Cancellation charges vary according to ticket type and proximity to travel date. ### What happens if you miss your train? - If you miss your reserved seat train, your ticket is **no longer valid and you will not be entitled to a refund.** This applies to Limited Express reserved seat tickets, Green Car tickets, sleeper cars and reserved seats. - Limited Express reserved seat tickets, however, **can be used for travel on non-reserved seats** on later trains on the same day as your missed train. Using reserved seating in this scenario incurs the full price of the Limited Express reserved seat fare. ## Select your seat preference and book your tickets Choose from various seat preferences on Shinkansen, limited express, and other trains. First-time bookers enjoy free seat selection! - ![Mt. Fuji view seats](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1ny0a12000t8at6quB911.jpg) ### Mt. Fuji view seats Selected window seats offering magnificent views of Mt. Fuji along the way. We recommend seats on the right for the Tokyo–Osaka route, or seats on the left for the Osaka–Tokyo route, subject to the specific train and direction. You can select Mt. Fuji view seats on Trip.com. - ![Oversized luggage seats (train end seats/rear seats)](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1ny6r12000t8asx16AAE9.jpg) ### Oversized luggage seats (train end seats/rear seats) Spacious seats located at the end of the car, close to the oversized luggage storage area for easy access to suitcases. Suitable for passengers with 26" or larger luggage. The lowest fare is $34.90, and the journey takes approx. 1h 23m. Reserved seat fares are slightly higher, and Green Car (first class) fares cost even more. You can check real-time fares for all available trains on our platform. - ### Do I need to reserve seats on bullet trains? __ Booking Shinkansen seats is optional, but recommended. Reserved seats guarantee a fixed seat and are included in the base fare (no extra charge). Most trains offer non-reserved seats (except Nozomi on some routes), but during peak times (holidays, commuter rush hours), non-reserved cars can be very crowded. If you want to guarantee a seat, sit with your companions, or travel during busy periods, please book in advance. You can book at station windows, ticket machines, or through our online booking platform. - ### Do Shinkansen trains run at night? __ Shinkansen trains generally operate from 06:16 to 22:08, and the last train time varies by route and direction. There are no night sleeper services on the Shinkansen. If you miss the last train, you can choose a night highway bus, stay at a nearby hotel, or take an airport bus—please plan your evening itinerary based on the last train time. - ### Can I use my Suica/IC card to pay for Shinkansen tickets? __ No—IC cards such as Suica, ICOCA, and PASMO cannot be used as Shinkansen tickets. Riding the Shinkansen requires you to separately purchase paper tickets or e-tickets (except for a small number of commuter IC fare products). However, IC cards can be used for regular trains, subways, and buses, as well as for purchases at station shops, convenience stores, and vending machines. To take the Shinkansen, please buy tickets online via Trip.com, or at station ticket windows or ticket machines. - ### Is there luggage storage at Shinkansen stations? __ Yes, most major Shinkansen stations provide coin lockers and staffed luggage storage counters. Lockers may be limited during peak travel times—please plan ahead. - ### How early should I book Shinkansen tickets? __ Tickets go on sale at 10:00 AM, exactly 1 month before departure. During peak travel seasons—such as Golden Week, Obon, and the New Year holidays—popular trains sell out quickly. We highly recommend booking the moment sales open to secure your seats. - ### Are Shinkansen stations wheelchair accessible? __ Yes, all major Shinkansen stations provide accessible passages, elevators, accessible restrooms, and accessible routes. Shinkansen trains feature designated wheelchair spaces. You can book assistance services in advance through JR or your travel agent for the smoothest experience. - ### How do overnight buses compare to Shinkansen? __ Yes, highway buses (night or day services) connect major cities and cost less than the Shinkansen. They are slower but offer great value for money. The popular long haul route from Tokyo to Nagano takes approx. 4h 40m. Wi-Fi and power outlets are usually provided on board. - ### Are there observation cars on Shinkansen? __ Some Shinkansen trains offer Green cars (first class) with panoramic windows or special observation seats. The Tokaido Shinkansen and some limited express trains feature scenic views along the route. For example, you can see Mount Fuji from a right-side seat on the Tokaido Shinkansen. - ### How can I see Mount Fuji from the Shinkansen? __ When riding the Tokaido Shinkansen, you can spot Mount Fuji between Shin-Yokohama Station and Shin-Fuji Station. Choose a seat on the side facing Mount Fuji (Seat E in standard cars and Seat D in Green cars). The best viewing window is within 3 minutes after passing Shin-Fuji Station. Clear days and winter months (December–February) offer the best views. As weather changes, visibility cannot be guaranteed. - ### Should I buy a new ticket if I miss my Shinkansen? __ Reserved seat tickets: You can take the next train on the same day, but you will need to sit in a non-reserved seat. If you wish to reserve a seat, please book a new express train ticket at the station. Non-reserved seat tickets: You can take the next train on the same day. - ### Can I eat on the Shinkansen? __ Passengers are allowed to eat on the Shinkansen. Most seats are equipped with cup holders and fold-out tables for convenient dining. Many passengers buy an ekiben (traditional Japanese railway bento) before boarding, which is a popular choice. You can also bring your own snacks and drinks. Please clean up after eating to keep the car clean. Eating on regular short-distance trains, however, is not in line with Japanese etiquette. - ### When to avoid trains in Japan? __ Peak times for train travel in Japan are approx. 7:00 AM–9:00 AM and 5:00 PM–7:30 PM on weekdays. The most crowded time is usually 8:00 AM–8:30 AM on inbound trains heading to central Tokyo and Osaka. Commuter lines can be extremely crowded, while Shinkansen and long-distance trains are usually much less affected. Additionally, please avoid peak travel seasons: Golden Week (late April to early May), Obon (mid-August), and New Year (Dec 29–Jan 3), when train demand is highest. For a comfortable experience, please travel during off-peak times and book seats in advance during busy periods. - ### What should I do if I miss my Shinkansen? __ If you miss your Shinkansen: Reserved seat tickets usually allow you to take the next train on the same day, but you can only ride in a non-reserved car. If you wish to guarantee a seat, you can book a new express train ticket at the station. Non-reserved seat tickets allow you to take the next train on the same day. Please note that unused tickets can usually be refunded before departure (a processing fee applies). Policies may vary by operator and fare type. Please view the ticket terms and conditions or inquire with station staff. - ### Is there Wi-Fi on Shinkansen trains? __ Most Shinkansen trains offer free Wi-Fi, including the Tokaido, Sanyo, Kyushu, Tohoku, Joetsu, Hokuriku, and Hokkaido lines (you can look for "Shinkansen\_WiFi" or an operator-specific SSID). Connection quality varies by region, especially in tunnels and rural areas. To ensure a stable Internet connection throughout your journey, we recommend preparing a travel eSIM or a portable Wi-Fi router as a backup. - ### How does the Shinkansen boarding process work? __ We recommend arriving at the station 30–45 minutes early. Find your platform on the departure information board, wait behind the yellow safety line on the platform, and board the car shown on your ticket. Use the same ticket to enter the station and to exit at your destination. - ### Can I use the JR Pass on Nozomi or Mizuho trains? __ The standard JR Pass is valid on Hikari, Kodama, Sakura, and Tsubame trains. Nozomi and Mizuho (the fastest services) require an additional Nozomi/Mizuho limited express ticket. Pass holders can ride these high-speed trains after paying the difference. - ### What is a women-only car on trains in Japan? __ Many commuter trains feature women-only cars. This is a safety measure during peak hours. The cars and active times are marked with bilingual signs in Japanese and English. Male passengers should avoid entering these cars during the designated periods. - ### Is there a tourist discount pass besides JR Pass? __ Yes, regional passes such as the Kansai Region Pass, Tokyo Metro Pass, and Hakone Pass offer considerable savings for specific areas. When traveling only within a city, topping up a Suica/ICOCA card is convenient and saves you from waiting in line to buy tickets. - ### Can I get a refund if my Shinkansen is canceled? __ If your train is canceled due to weather or operational issues, you can usually get a full refund or change your ticket for free. You can contact JR staff at the station, or if you booked on Trip.com, contact customer support for assistance. Specific policies vary by operator and fare type. - ### Is English spoken on Shinkansen trains? __ Most Shinkansen announcements are bilingual in Japanese and English. Staff at major stations speak some English. Translation apps and signs are helpful for navigation. Train attendants' English might be limited. A translation app or phrasebook is very helpful when making specific requests. - ### Can I cancel or change one person's ticket in a group booking? __ Partial cancellation is supported. You can cancel individual passengers in a group booking. Partial changes are only supported by some suppliers. Please refer to your ticket policies for details. - ### What are the luggage restrictions on the Shinkansen? __ The maximum luggage size for all JR trains is 250 cm (length + width + height). Only the Tokaido, Sanyo, Kyushu, and Nishi-Kyushu Shinkansen require you to reserve luggage seats in advance. Luggage with total dimensions of 160–250 cm (length + width + height) requires dedicated space. If you bring oversized luggage without reserving in advance, you will be charged a fee of JPY 1,000. ## Why book Japan rail tickets on Trip.com? - ![Japan Rail official partner](https://dimg04.tripcdn.com/images/1op4z12000m1hy64d6E98.png) ### Japan Rail official partner A platform you can trust with a complete travel guide - ![Extensive coverage](https://dimg04.tripcdn.com/images/1op6k12000lye0nn0BD17.png) ### Extensive coverage Includes JR lines and non-Shinkansen trains - ![Online changes](https://dimg04.tripcdn.com/images/1op4112000m1hzuuc0518.png) ### Online changes Exclusive online ticket changes available, no need to line up at the station - ![Multilingual support](https://dimg04.tripcdn.com/images/1op6r12000m1hyue2B23C.png) ### Multilingual support Information in 13 languages, real-time updates in 4 languages ## Train stations near me Find nearby stations ## Recommendations 1. ### Shinkansen from Tokyo 1. Plan your trip to Tokyo ## Information about the Nagano to Tokyo train route The Nagano to Tokyo train route is one of the most convenient and scenic rail connections in Japan, linking the mountain city of Nagano with the capital via the Hokuriku Shinkansen (also known as the Nagano Shinkansen corridor). Nagano Station is located at 1106 Kurita, Nagano City, Nagano Prefecture 380-0921, while Tokyo Station sits at 1-9-1 Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 100-0005, one of Japan's busiest and best-connected transport hubs. The route follows a corridor that cuts through the Japanese Alps, offering passengers striking mountain scenery before descending into the greater Tokyo metropolitan area. It was originally developed and expanded ahead of the 1998 Nagano Winter Olympics, which put the city firmly on the international map. Today, the Nagano to Tokyo bullet train remains one of the most popular shinkansen connections for both domestic travelers and international visitors heading to or from the Japanese Alps. Two Shinkansen services operate on this route: the **Kagayaki**, which runs express with minimal stops, and the **Hakutaka**, which makes more stops along the Hokuriku corridor. For travelers going directly between Nagano and Tokyo, the **Kagayaki** is typically the fastest option, while the **Hakutaka** offers more flexibility for those stopping at intermediate stations. We recommend using the JR Pass for traveling in trains all around Japan to save more money if you plan to do many trips. Trains depart from Nagano Station's dedicated Shinkansen platforms, which are clearly signposted in both Japanese and English, making navigation easy even for first-time visitors. **Seating options** - **Ordinary Class (Ordinary Car)**, comfortable, well-spaced seating that is perfectly adequate for this route. Clean, quiet, and a smooth ride throughout. - **Green Car (first class)**, wider seats, additional legroom, and a noticeably quieter carriage. A worthwhile upgrade if you prefer extra comfort or are traveling with bulkier luggage. - **Gran Class**, available on select Kagayaki services, offering premium reclining seats with a meal and drink service included. An excellent option if you want to make the journey itself feel like part of the experience. **Best seats for the view** The Nagano to Tokyo shinkansen passes through some spectacular scenery as it descends from the mountains toward the Kanto plain. To make the most of the views: - Sit on the **left-hand side of the train** (A window seats) when traveling from Nagano toward Tokyo for the best views of the mountain landscapes in the early part of the journey. - The most dramatic alpine scenery appears in the **first 20 to 30 minutes** after departing Nagano, as the train moves through the foothills of the Japanese Alps. - On clear days, the contrast between the snowy peaks and the valleys below is particularly striking in **winter and early spring**. **On-board experience** Like all Shinkansen services in Japan, the Nagano to Tokyo bullet train is clean, punctual, and pleasantly quiet. Mobile phone calls are discouraged in the carriages, keeping the atmosphere calm. A trolley service passes through the train selling drinks, light snacks, and packaged goods. However, a far more rewarding option is to pick up a regional **ekiben** (station bento box) at Nagano Station before boarding, the station has several vendors offering bento featuring local Nagano specialties such as oyaki-inspired flavors and mountain vegetable dishes. **Best time of year to travel** - **Winter (December to February):** Nagano is one of Japan's premier ski destinations, home to resorts such as Hakuba, Shiga Kogen, and Nozawa Onsen. Trains are busiest on Friday evenings heading from Tokyo to Nagano and Sunday afternoons in the return direction. Book ahead during ski season. - **Spring (late March to early May):** Cherry blossoms arrive slightly later in Nagano than in Tokyo due to the higher altitude, creating a beautiful contrast. A quieter time to travel compared to peak ski season. - **Autumn (mid-October to late November):** The foliage in the Nagano region is outstanding, particularly around Jigokudani Monkey Park and the Togakushi area. Trains can fill up on weekends during peak foliage weeks. - **Summer (July to August):** Nagano's cooler mountain climate makes it a popular escape from Tokyo's heat and humidity. A comfortable season to travel in both directions. ## Getting to Tokyo and beyond Tokyo Station is one of the most comprehensively connected transport hubs in the world, and arriving there from Nagano places you within easy reach of virtually every corner of Japan as well as the wider Tokyo metropolitan area. **Within Tokyo** Tokyo Station connects directly to multiple JR lines, the Tokyo Metro, and the Marunouchi subway line. Key connections from Tokyo Station include: - **Yamanote Line**, the circular loop connecting major Tokyo hubs including Shinjuku, Shibuya, Harajuku, Ueno, and Akihabara. - **Chuo Line**, fast access westward toward Shinjuku and beyond. - **Keiyo Line**, connections toward Tokyo Disneyland (Maihama Station) and the waterfront areas. - **Narita Express (N'EX)**, direct trains to Narita International Airport, ideal if you are connecting onward internationally. - **Limousine Bus services**, available from directly outside the station to Haneda Airport. **Day trips and regional connections from Tokyo** Tokyo Station is also the departure point for Shinkansen services in almost every direction, making it an ideal base for wider exploration: - **Kyoto and Osaka**, reached via the Tokaido Shinkansen, one of Japan's busiest rail corridors. - **Hakone**, a popular day trip accessible via the Odakyu Romance Car from Shinjuku or the JR Tokaido Line to Odawara. - **Nikko**, around 2 hours by train from Tokyo, offering stunning temples and mountain scenery. - **Kanazawa**, accessible via the Hokuriku Shinkansen in the opposite direction from Nagano, a worthwhile addition to any Japan itinerary. # How to Get to Nagano from Tokyo: Shinkansen, Bus, Car or RV?

2025.10.13

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/4356562_m.jpg)

Nagano is one of Japan’s top destinations for international travelers, famous for its ski resorts, hot springs, historic temples, and stunning mountain scenery. But if you’re planning your trip, you may be asking yourself: how to get to Nagano from Tokyo in the fastest, most affordable, or most flexible way?

In this guide, we’ll compare the four main options—Shinkansen (bullet train), highway bus, rental car, and RV rental—so you can decide which suits your travel style best. Whether you want speed, budget savings, or a once-in-a-lifetime road trip adventure, you’ll find the answer here.

[Reservation](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/tokyo/item-reserve/?lang=en)

## Travel Options from Tokyo to Nagano (Quick Comparison)

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/33432652_m.jpg)

**Here’s a quick look at the main travel options from Tokyo to Nagano:**

| Transport | Approx. Travel Time\* | Approx. Cost\* | Highlights |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shinkansen | 1.5 hours | ¥6,000~¥10,000 per person | Fastest and most comfortable, but limited luggage space |
| Highway Bus | 4~5 hours | ¥3,500~¥6,000 per person | Cheapest option, but takes more time |
| Car | 3~4hours | Expressway tolls + fuel | High flexibility, ideal for group travel |
| RV Rental | 3~4 hours | Rental fee + expressway tolls + fuel + RV park fees | Combines transport, accommodation, and sightseeing in one |

\\* Travel time and cost estimates are based on standard conditions and may vary with season, traffic, or route.

**Key Takeaways:**

- ・Choose the Shinkansen if speed matters most.
- ・Choose a highway bus if you’re traveling on a budget.
- ・Choose a car or RV if you want flexibility and scenic stops.
- ・For ski trips or heavy luggage, RVs offer unique advantages.

## 1\. Taking the Shinkansen from Tokyo to Nagano

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/32724150_m.jpg)

**Route Overview**

- ・The Hokuriku Shinkansen directly connects Tokyo Station with Nagano Station. ( [JR East official route map](https://www.jreast.co.jp/en/multi/routemaps/hokurikushinkansen.html))
- ・Different train categories include Kagayaki (fastest, fewest stops), Hakutaka (stops at more stations), and Asama (serves local stations). ( [Japan Guide](https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2018_nagano.html))

**Travel Time**

- ・Fastest option: around 1 hour 20 minutes (Kagayaki service).
- ・Slower services may take up to 1 hour 40 minutes, depending on stops. ( [Japan Experience](https://www.japan-experience.com/transportation/train-tickets/train-ticket-tokyo-nagano))

**Ticket Prices**

- ・Standard reserved/unreserved seats: around ¥7,000–~¥9,000 one way.
- ・Green Car (first-class) tickets cost more.
- ・Tickets can be booked online via the official [JR East Train Reservation](https://www.eki-net.com/en/jreast-train-reservation/Top/Index) system.

**How to Book & Use**

- ・Tickets go on sale one month before departure; book early during peak travel seasons (ski season, holidays).
- ・Departures are from Tokyo Station’s Shinkansen platforms (look for signs for Hokuriku Shinkansen).
- ・Tickets can be purchased at “Midori no Madoguchi” (Ticket Office) counters or ticket machines with English options.
- ・Holders of the Japan Rail Pass can ride this route at no extra cost (check pass validity).

**Advantages / Disadvantages**

**Advantages:**

- ・Fastest and most reliable option.
- ・Comfortable ride with spacious seats and luggage racks.
- ・Arrives directly in Nagano City, close to Zenkoji Temple and local transport.


**Disadvantages:**

- ・Higher cost compared to buses.
- ・Limited convenience if your destination is outside Nagano City (e.g., Hakuba ski resorts or hot spring villages).
- ・Ski gear and bulky luggage can be inconvenient to carry on board, and there are also luggage restrictions.


**Best For:**

- ・Travelers on a tight schedule.
- ・Visitors focusing on Nagano City (Zenkoji Temple, local food, culture).
- ・Those who prefer stress-free public transport over driving.

## 2\. Taking a Highway Bus from Tokyo to Nagano

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/4331730_m.jpg)

**Route Overview**

- ・Highway buses run between Tokyo (Shinjuku, Ikebukuro, or Tokyo Station) and Nagano Station.
- ・Major operators include Alpico Group and Keio Bus, offering both daytime and overnight buses. ( [Alpico Bus Official](https://www.alpico.co.jp/en/))

**Travel Time**

- ・Average journey: 4 to 5 hours, depending on traffic conditions.
- ・Overnight buses are available, arriving in Nagano early in the morning—ideal for ski travelers heading directly to the slopes.

**Ticket Prices**

- ・Fares typically range from ¥3,500~¥6,000 one way, making it the most budget-friendly option.
- ・Advance booking is recommended during ski season and holidays. Tickets can be purchased online or at bus terminals.

- **Advantages / Disadvantages**

**Advantages:**

- ・Cheapest way to travel from Tokyo to Nagano.
- ・Overnight buses help save on accommodation costs.
- ・Direct arrivals at Nagano Station, with some services continuing to Hakuba ski resorts.

**Disadvantages:**

- ・Longer travel time than the Shinkansen.
- ・Limited comfort compared to trains (especially on daytime trips).
- ・Traffic delays are possible, especially during winter.

**Best For:**

- ・Budget-conscious travelers.
- ・Solo backpackers or students.
- ・Travelers who don’t mind longer journeys in exchange for saving money.

## 3\. Driving a Car from Tokyo to Nagano

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/33146606_m.jpg)

**Route Overview**

- ・Driving offers full freedom to stop at Mount Fuji, Karuizawa, or roadside attractions along the way.
- ・The most common route is via the Kan-Etsu Expressway or Joshin-Etsu Expressway.

**Travel Time**

- ・3 to 4 hours, depending on traffic and rest stops.
- ・In winter, snow and ice can extend travel times by affecting road conditions.

**Costs**

- ・Expressway tolls: approx. ¥4,000~¥6,000 one way, depending on entry/exit points.
- ・Fuel: approx. ¥3,000~¥5,000 for the journey.
- ・Rental car prices vary, starting at ¥8,000~¥12,000 per day for compact cars, if you choose to rent a car.


**Advantages / Disadvantages**

**Advantages:**

- ・Total flexibility—you decide when to stop, detour, or explore.
- ・Convenient for families with kids or groups with luggage.
- ・Easy access to off-the-beaten-path spots like mountain onsens or Kamikochi.

**Disadvantages:**

- ・Expressway tolls and fuel add up quickly.
- ・Winter driving requires snow tires or chains, plus caution on icy roads.
- ・Parking fees in cities and tourist areas.

**Best For:**

- ・Families and small groups traveling together.
- ・Those who want to combine a trip to Nagano with sightseeing stops along the way.
- ・Confident drivers comfortable with Japanese road rules.

## 4.Renting an RV from Tokyo to Nagano

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/TOP4.jpg)

- **Route Overview**
- ・With an RV, your journey from Tokyo to Nagano is not just about getting there—it’s part of the adventure.
- ・AROUND JAPAN RV ( [official site](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/)) offers vehicles fully equipped with beds, kitchen, heating, and solar power.

**Travel Time**

- ・Similar to a car: 3 to 4 hours, depending on traffic and stops.
- ・RV travel is often slower due to scenic detours and overnight stays at roadside stations or RV parks.

**Costs**

- ・Rental fee: approx. ¥27,000~¥34,000 per day (regular season, incl. tax)  ( [pricing details](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/tokyo/price/)).
- ・Fuel: diesel-powered RVs average 7~9 km/L, so expect ¥4,000–¥6,000 for the drive to Nagano.
- ・Expressway tolls: ¥4,000~¥6,000 one way.
- ・RV parks or Michi-no-Eki (roadside stations): ¥3,000~¥5,000 per night, often with hot springs nearby.

**Advantages / Disadvantages**

**Advantages:**

- ・Combines transport + accommodation, reducing hotel costs.
- ・Freedom to bring ski/snowboard gear without worrying about luggage limits.
- ・Stay overnight in nature, by hot springs, or near ski resorts.
- ・Perfect for families or groups of friends.

**Disadvantages:**

- ・Higher upfront cost than buses or trains.
- ・Larger vehicle requires careful driving, especially in narrow streets.
- ・Campsite or RV park reservations may be needed during peak ski season.


**Best For:**

- ・Skiers and snowboarders with lots of gear.
- ・Families or groups seeking flexibility.
- ・Travelers who want the journey itself to be part of the experience.
- ・Adventurers who enjoy stargazing, cooking, or discovering rural Japan.

**Want to learn more? See our detailed guides:**

- ・RV Rental for a Week in Japan: Costs, Routes, and Tips for Travelers
- ・RV Rental for 2 Weeks in Japan: Costs, Routes, and Long-Term Travel Tips
- ・Small RV Rentals in Japan: Prices, Benefits, and Travel Ideas

[Reservation](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/tokyo/item-reserve/?lang=en)

## Getting Around Nagano: Access to Major Attractions

Once you arrive at Nagano Station by Shinkansen, bus, or car, the next step is reaching the prefecture’s world-famous sights. Here’s a breakdown of how to get to key destinations using public transport vs. rental car, with pros and cons for each.

### 1\. Zenkoji Temple

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/29322688_m.jpg)

**Overview:**

Nagano’s most important cultural landmark, Zenkoji Temple, is located in the city itself.

- From Nagano Station: approx. 2 km.

**Access Options:**

- ・Bus: 10 minutes, approx. ¥150~¥200. Buses run every few minutes from the east exit.
- ・Taxi: 5 minutes, approx. ¥1,000.
- ・On foot: 20~25 minutes, walking straight up Chuo-dori Avenue.

**Pros & Cons:**

- ・Bus: Cheap and easy, though you might have to wait a while.
- ・Car: Not necessary; parking near the temple is limited and often crowded.
- ・Best choice: Walking or bus.

- **Link:**
- [Zenkoji Temple Official Site](https://www.zenkoji.jp/en/)

### 2\. Jigokudani Monkey Park (Snow Monkeys)

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/4356562_m.jpg)

**Overview:**

Home to the famous hot spring–bathing monkeys in Yamanouchi.

- From Nagano Station:

**Train + Bus:**

- ・Nagano → Yudanaka (Limited Express, approx. 45 min, ¥1,290).
- ・Yudanaka → Kanbayashi Onsen (local bus, approx. 10 min, ¥310).
- ・Walk 30 minutes from the bus stop to the park.
- ・Total: 1 hour or a bit more one way, ¥1,600 (approx).

**Direct Express Bus:**

- ・Nagano → Snow Monkey Park entrance.
- ・42 min, ¥2,000 one way. ( [Nagaden Bus Info](https://www.nagaden-net.co.jp.e.yv.hp.transer.com/snowmonkeyresorts))

**Car/RV Rental:**

- ・About 50 minutes via Joshin-Etsu Expressway.
- ・Parking available near the trailhead (¥500).

**Pros & Cons:**

- ・Train + Bus: Scenic, but requires multiple transfers and a 30-minute uphill walk.
- ・Direct Bus: Easiest by public transport, but limited departures.
- ・Car/RV Rental: Flexible and faster if traveling with family or luggage.

**Link:**

- [Jigokudani Yaen-Koen Official Site](https://en.jigokudani-yaenkoen.co.jp/)

### 3\. Hakuba (Ski Resorts & Winter Sports)

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/23012029_m.jpg)

**Overview:**

Hakuba Valley in Nagano Prefecture is a world-famous ski and snowboard destination. Travelers coming from Nagano City can reach Hakuba by bus, train, car or RV Rental.

**From Nagano Station:**

**Express Bus (Alpico Bus):**

Direct service to Hakuba Happo Bus Terminal.

- ・Journey time: 70~90 minutes, depending on the route
- ・Fare: ¥2,200~¥2,400 one way

**Train + Oito Line Route:**

- ・Nagano → Matsumoto (JR, time varies by train type)
- ・Matsumoto → Hakuba (JR Oito Line, 95~120 min, ¥1,170)
- ・Total: 2.5~3 hours depending on connections

**Car/RV Rental:**

- ・Approx. 1.5~2 hours drive via Nagano Expressway and Route 148 (depending on traffic)
- ・Parking widely available at ski resorts (fees vary by resort)

**Pros & Cons:**

- ・Express Bus: Convenient and direct, but operates on a fixed schedule.
- ・Train + Oito Line: Scenic and reliable, but involves a transfer at Matsumoto and longer travel time.
- ・Car / RV Rental: Offers maximum flexibility—perfect for carrying ski gear or detouring to nearby onsen towns—but driving in winter may require caution.

- **Links:**
- [Hakuba Tourism Official Site](https://hakuba-tourism.com/)
- [Hakuba Village Official Site](https://vill-hakuba.nagano.jp/)
- [Hakuba Happo Onsen](https://hakuba-happo-onsen.jp/english/)

### 4\. Matsumoto (Castle Town & Gateway to the Alps)

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/33509651_m.jpg)

**Overview:**

Nagano → Matsumoto is a popular extension trip to see Matsumoto Castle.

**From Nagano Station:**

**Train (JR Shinonoi Line / Limited Express Shinano):** 50~70 min depending on train type.

- ・Local trains are cheaper (¥1,170 one way), but slower.
- ・Limited Express Shinano trains are faster (50~55 min) with higher fares (¥2,500~¥3,000 depending on seat class).

**Bus:** Some highway buses run between Nagano and Matsumoto. Travel time is about 60~90 min, fares around ¥2,000 (varies by operator and season).

**Car/RV Rental:** About 1~1.5 hrs drive (60~70 km). Fuel + tolls typically ¥2,000~¥3,000 for a standard vehicle, depending on route and fuel prices.

**Pros & Cons:**

- **・Train:** Reliable, frequent departures, and no transfers needed.
- **・Bus:** Comfortable and direct when available, but less frequent than trains.
- **・Car / RV Rental:** Most flexible—ideal if you want to explore nearby spots such as Azumino, hot spring towns, or Kamikochi (accessible seasonally).

- **Link:**
- [Matsumoto Castle Official Site](https://www.matsumoto-castle.jp/eng)

### 5\. Kamikochi (Japan Alps Scenic Valley)

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/33206547_m.jpg)

**Overview:**

Kamikochi is a breathtaking alpine valley inside Chubu Sangaku National Park, famous for hiking and nature. Private cars cannot enter Kamikochi directly — you must transfer to a bus or taxi at designated parking areas.

**From Nagano Station:**

**Train + Bus route (via Matsumoto → Shin-Shimashima):**

- ・Nagano → Matsumoto (JR) 50~70 minutes, approx. ¥1,170 (depending on train type)
- ・Matsumoto → Shin-Shimashima (Alpico Line): approx. 30 minutes, ¥710
- ・Shin-Shimashima → Kamikochi (Alpico Bus): approx. 60~70 minutes, ¥2,570
- ・Total travel time: approx. 3 hours (excluding transfers), cost approx. ¥4,400 one way

- **Highway Bus (seasonal):**


  - ・Direct bus Nagano → Kamikochi (mid-April to mid-Nov).
  - ・Approx. 2 hrs 40 min ~ 3 hrs, ¥4,500 one way.
- **Car/RV Rental:**


  - ・Approx. 3 hours’ drive from Nagano to Sawando Parking
- ・Parking at Sawando: ¥600 per day
- ・From Sawando → Kamikochi: shuttle bus or taxi (30~40 minutes, ¥1,000 one way by bus)

**Pros & Cons:**

- **・Train + Bus:** Scenic and reliable, but requires multiple transfers
- **・Direct Bus:** The easiest option when in season, but limited operation (mid-April–mid-November only)
- **・Car / RV Rental:** Most flexible, especially for groups or families, but private vehicles cannot enter Kamikochi—requires parking and a shuttle transfer

- **Link:**
- [Kamikochi Official Website](https://www.kamikochi.org/)

## Which is the Best Way to Travel from Tokyo to Nagano?

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/aj_slide5.jpg)

When choosing how to get from Tokyo to Nagano, travelers usually consider speed, cost, and convenience. Each option—Shinkansen, bus, rental car, or RV—has its strengths:

- **・Shinkansen:** fastest, 1.5 hours, convenient for solo travelers or tight schedules.
- **・Bus:** budget-friendly, 4~5 hours, good for travelers prioritizing cost over time.
- **・Car/RV Rental:** flexible, 3~4 hours, great for groups or sightseeing stops along the way.


But if you want more than just a point-to-point transfer, renting an RV from Tokyo to Nagano offers a unique, immersive travel experience that combines transportation, accommodation, and adventure.

### 1\. Travel + Accommodation + Experience in One

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Image.jpeg)

**With an RV from [AROUND JAPAN](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/), the journey itself becomes part of your trip:**

- **・Scenic drives:** Enjoy stunning views of Mount Fuji, the Japanese Alps, and rural landscapes along the way.
- **・Flexible overnight stays:** Park at Michi-no-Eki roadside stations, RV parks, or near ski resorts and hot springs.
- **・Home on wheels:** Fully equipped RVs with beds, kitchen, and heating mean you can cook, sleep, and relax anywhere.

Unlike the Shinkansen or bus, which simply take you from place to place, an RV lets you experience Japan at your own pace.

### 2\. Perfect for Nagano’s Seasonal Attractions

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/tg_activity.jpg)

**Nagano is famous for winter sports, onsen, and alpine nature. RVs are uniquely suited for these experiences:**

- **・Ski & snowboard trips:** Bring your gear directly—no luggage limits. Stop at multiple resorts in a single trip.
- **・Hot spring hopping:** Visit Happo Onsen, Kamikochi area onsens, or hidden alpine baths with ease.
- **・Nature immersion:** Wake up near snow-capped mountains or pristine rivers, and enjoy hiking, stargazing, or early morning landscapes.

The RV transforms a simple transfer into an adventure tailored to outdoor enthusiasts and families.

### 3\. Unmatched Freedom & Flexibility

![conveniently drop off your RV in Osaka before flying home](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/A2.jpg)

- ・Decide your route on the fly: Detour to Matsumoto Castle, Zenkoji Temple, or Jigokudani Monkey Park without worrying about train schedules.
- ・Travel with groups or family: Large RVs accommodate 4~6 people comfortably—ideal for shared adventures.
- ・Discover local culture: Stop at roadside markets, small towns, or seasonal festivals that are off the main tourist routes.

In short, an RV gives you complete control over your trip, something impossible with fixed-schedule transport.

## Conclusion: Travel from Tokyo to Nagano with Freedom and Ease

![](https://aroundjapan-rv.com/en/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/33582650_m.jpg)

**Getting from Tokyo to Nagano offers multiple options:**

- ・Shinkansen: Fastest, convenient for solo travelers or short schedules.
- ・Highway Bus: Budget-friendly, suitable for cost-conscious travelers.
- ・Car: Flexible for sightseeing along the way.
- ・RV Rental: Combines travel, accommodation, and adventure in one seamless experience.


While the Shinkansen and bus offer efficient travel, an RV transforms the journey itself into a memorable experience, with stops at scenic vistas, alpine landscapes, and hidden gems along the way.

Nagano’s attractions—Zenkoji Temple, Jigokudani Monkey Park, Matsumoto Castle, Kamikochi, and Hakuba ski resorts—are easily accessible by RV, giving you the freedom to explore at your own pace.

## Narita Express service area (Narita Express stop)

## Narita Express Information

![Narita Express](https://www.jreast.co.jp/multi/nex/img/nex_img01.jpg)

We have adopted universal design principles in line with the brand image of N'EX (airport limited express) to create comfort and security.

### Facilities

Features and a design suited for limited express access to airports. In-car facilities have been further enhanced, making transportation from Narita Airport even more comfortable.

#### Luggage storage area \*No reservation required

![](https://www.jreast.co.jp/multi/nex/img/facilities_img07.jpg)

![](https://www.jreast.co.jp/multi/nex/img/facilities_img08.jpg)

Security cameras are installed near the doorways and in the luggage compartment areas. The luggage compartment areas of each train is fitted with a dial-type lock. Additionally, we are installing emergency alert devices in the trains that allow for communication with crew members to improve security.

#### Multilingual support available

![](https://www.jreast.co.jp/multi/nex/img/facilities_img01.jpg)

![](https://www.jreast.co.jp/multi/nex/img/facilities_img02.jpg)

Installed onboard are large LCD guidance devices that provide information including information about destinations, service statuses, news, weather reports, and flight information (inbound trains) in four languages (English, Chinese, Korean, and Japanese).

\\* Some content is only available in two languages (English and Japanese).

#### Safe for wheelchair users and those with children

![](https://www.jreast.co.jp/multi/nex/img/facilities_img03.jpg)Multipurpose room

![](https://www.jreast.co.jp/multi/nex/img/facilities_img04.jpg)Large Western-style toilet

![](https://www.jreast.co.jp/multi/nex/img/facilities_img05.jpg)The Western-style toilets are equipped with baby beds and baby chairs.

![](https://www.jreast.co.jp/multi/nex/img/facilities_img06.jpg)Braille signage (doorways and toilets)

Many accessibility-related measures have been implemented including a large Western-style toilet for users of electric wheelchairs, low-hanging luggage racks, and minimized gaps between platforms and trains.

### Seat

The N'EX is made up of Green Cars (first class) and Ordinary Cars. Please relax in the comfortable interior and as appropriate to what you require.

#### Green Car (first class)

![](https://www.jreast.co.jp/multi/nex/img/seating_img01.jpg)

![](https://www.jreast.co.jp/multi/nex/img/seating_img02.jpg)

![](https://www.jreast.co.jp/multi/nex/img/seating_img03.jpg)

Ordinary seat features

- Large seat table

- Leg room (H = 250 mm)

## FAQ

Q.

Where should I store my luggage on the Narita Express? Is a reservation required?

A.

The Narita Express has overhead luggage racks and storage areas for large luggage.

The large luggage area does not require a reservation.

However, space is limited, so it is available on a first-come, first-served basis.

Depending on the size and shape of your luggage, it may not fit.

If the large luggage area is full, please place your luggage at your feet.

If you are bringing large luggage on board, please also check the [Oversized Luggage Guide.](https://www.jreast.co.jp/en/multi/luggage-area/) ​

For more information, please call the number below.

JR East Infoline (available in Japanese, English, Chinese, and Korean)050-2016-1603（JST 10:00 -18:00）International calls from overseas: +81-50-2016-1603

Q.

Which stations does the Narita Express stop at?

A.

For details about Narita Express stops, please go [here](https://www.jreast.co.jp/en/multi/nex/#nex_routemap).

Q.

Where can the N'EX TOKYO Round Trip Ticket be picked up?

A.

This ticket can only be picked up at

Narita Airport Terminal 1 Station or

Narita Airport Terminal 2・3 Station.

You can pick up your ticket at the following locations:

- • JR EAST Travel Service Center and JR Ticket Office (Midori-no-Madoguchi) counters
- • Ticket vending machines with passport readers (reserved seat ticket vending machines equipped with passport readers)

You can also make same-day seat reservations at JR EAST Travel Service Center and JR Ticket Office (Midori-no-Madoguchi) counters and ticket vending machines equipped with passport readers at stations inside Narita Airport.

Narita Airport Terminal 1 Station

- • JR EAST Travel Service Center (8:30–19:00)
- • Ticket vending machines with passport readers (reserved seat ticket vending machines equipped with passport readers) (6:30–21:45)
- • JR Ticket Offices (Midori-no-Madoguchi) (6:30–21:45)
[Station MapOpens in a new window](https://www.jreast.co.jp/en/e/stations/e1130.html)


Narita Airport Terminal 2・3 Station

- • JR EAST Travel Service Centers (8:30–20:00)
- • Ticket vending machines with passport readers (reserved seat ticket vending machines equipped with passport readers) (6:30–21:45)
- • JR Ticket Offices (Midori-no-Madoguchi) (6:30–21:45)
[Station MapOpens in a new window](https://www.jreast.co.jp/en/e/stations/e611.html)


For more information, see the [N'EX TOKYO Round Trip Ticket](https://www.jreast.co.jp/en/multi/pass/nex.html) page.

Q.

Do the outbound and return rides on the N'EX TOKYO Round Trip Ticket have to be between the same stations?

For example:

- • Outbound: Narita Airport Terminal 1 Station → Shinjuku Station
- • Return: Tōkyō Station → Narita Airport Terminal 1 Station

A.

No, they do not have to be between the same stations.

For example:

- • Outbound: Narita Airport Terminal 1 Station → Shinjuku Station
- • Return: Tōkyō Station → Narita Airport Terminal 1 Station

As shown above, you can use the ticket for different stations.

However, there are rules for how the ticket can be used.

- • For the outbound trip, use the ticket from Narita Airport → Tokyo (Central Tokyo: Tokyo and the surrounding area, including Yokohama and Ōfuna)
- • For the return trip, use the ticket from Tokyo (Central Tokyo: Tokyo and the surrounding area, including Yokohama and Ōfuna) → Narita Airport

.

The reverse is not permitted (Tokyo → Narita Airport for the outbound trip and Narita Airport → Tokyo for the return trip).

For more information, see the [N'EX TOKYO Round Trip Ticket](https://www.jreast.co.jp/en/multi/pass/nex.html#pass_availableArea) page.

Q.

Can I use the N'EX TOKYO Round Trip Ticket to ride other trains on the same day I ride the Narita Express?

A.

The N'EX TOKYO Round Trip Ticket is not an unlimited pass.

You can only use it twice.

(Example)

- • First trip: Narita Airport → JR stations in Tokyo and the surrounding area
- • Second trip: JR stations in Tokyo and the surrounding area → Narita Airport

After riding the Narita Express, you can transfer to other JR trains and travel to any station covered by the ticket at no extra cost as long as you do not exit the ticket gates.

The same applies to the return trip. As long as you do not exit the ticket gates, you can transfer from another JR train to the Narita Express.

\*Note

Once you exit the ticket gates, the ticket can no longer be used.

For details on the area covered by the ticket, please see the [N'EX TOKYO Round Trip Ticket](https://www.jreast.co.jp/en/multi/pass/nex.html) page.

Q.

I reserved a Narita Express ticket through JR-EAST Train Reservation. What should I do if my flight is delayed and I miss my reserved train?

A.

If you think you may miss your train or expect to arrive early, please visit the JR East [website(Opens in a new window)](https://www.eki-net.com/en/jreast-train-reservation/Top/Index) to cancel your current reservation and reserve a different train. For details on cancellation deadlines and refund fees (fees charged when you receive a ticket refund), please see the [Refund Fees (for ticket refunds) page (Opens in a new window)](https://www.eki-net.com/top/tr/guide/change/#c-headerAcc_02_01).

If you miss your reserved train, you can take a later train on the same day without changing your ticket.

However, you will not have an assigned seat. Please take any available seat.

If a passenger with a reservation for that seat arrives, you must give up the seat.

To make the journey, you can choose between several different travel options, depending on your budget and preference. ## Fastest Option: Tokyo to Nagano by Hokuriku Shinkansen The Hokuriku Shinkansen is the fastest and most convenient way to travel from Tokyo to Nagano. ![A Japanese Shinkansen bullet train speeds past a field of pink flowers with the snow-capped Mount Fuji in the background under a blue sky](https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/wp-content/uploads/Hokuiruku-Shinkansen.webp)A Shinkansen bullet train passing a flower field near Mount Fuji (via KKday Supplier) In as little as 80 minutes, you’ll go from Tokyo to the mountains of Nagano. This is ideal for day trips, weekend getaways, and ski holidays. ### Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen Travel Time & Cost | | | | | --- | --- | --- | | **Service** | **Travel Time** | **Cost** | | **Kagayaki** | ~80 min | ¥8,000–¥9,500 | | **Hakutaka** | ~90–95 min | ¥8,000–¥9,500 | | **Asama** | ~100 min | ¥8,000–¥9,500 | ### Kagayaki vs. Hakutaka vs. Asama At-A-Glance When you look at the departure boards at the station, you’ll notice three distinct train names operating along this line. Knowing which one to book keeps your schedule tightly optimized: | | | | --- | --- | | **Kagayaki (The Lightning Express)** | Fastest option with limited stops (Ueno, Omiya, and Nagano). Reserved seats only. | | **Hakutaka (The Flexible Cruiser)** | Slightly slower but offers both reserved and non-reserved seating. | | **Asama (The Local Shuttle)** | Makes the most stops but is a good alternative when other trains are full. | ### Tokyo Station or Ueno Station? [![A woman from behind wearing a yellow skirt standing in the large plaza outside the historic red brick facade of Tokyo Station under a clear blue sky](https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/wp-content/uploads/Tokyo-Station-260x195.webp)](https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/97503/tokyo-to-yokohama-transit/tokyo-station-2) [![The exterior building facade of Ueno Station in Tokyo featuring green signage on the roof and a spacious tiled pedestrian terrace in the foreground](https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/wp-content/uploads/Ueno-station-260x195.webp)](https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/97534/tokyo-to-nagano-travel/ueno-station) You can board the Hokuriku Shinkansen from two major hubs in central Tokyo. Choosing the right one saves you from dragging heavy luggage across city subways: | | | | --- | --- | | **Tokyo Station** | Best for securing non-reserved seats since it’s the starting station. | | **Ueno Station** | More convenient if you’re staying around Ueno, Asakusa, or Akihabara. | ### Reserved vs. Non-Reserved Seats Choosing between a reserved seat (Shitei-seki) and a non-reserved seat (Jiyu-seki) comes down to peace of mind versus budget flexibility: | | | | --- | --- | | **Reserved Seat** | **Non-Reserved Seat** | | Guaranteed seat assignment | More flexibility | | Recommended during busy travel periods | Available on Hakutaka and Asama trains | | Ideal for groups and travelers with luggage | May require standing if trains are crowded | ### Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen: Quick Boarding Guide 1. **Purchase or collect your ticket** via KKday, at the green JR Ticket Office (Midori-no-Madoguchi), or via the touchscreen digital ticket machines at Tokyo or Ueno Station. 2. **Enter through the Shinkansen gates** by inserting your physical ticket into the automated Shinkansen turnstiles. Remember to grab it as it pops out the other side! 3. **Follow the bright green Hokuriku Shinkansen signs** to your designated platform. 4. **Queue at your assigned car number**. If you have an unreserved ticket, line up early in the designated Jiyu-seki lanes. 5. **Store your luggage** in the overhead racks or designated luggage spaces. 6. **Enjoy the ride** and arrive at Nagano Station in around 80–100 minutes. | | | | --- | --- | | **KKday Editor’s Tips** | Popular departures can sell out quickly. | | **Book as early as possible** (around 30 days prior) if you’re traveling during ski season (December–March), cherry blossom season, Golden Week, or autumn foliage season. | [Check Remaining Seats – Reserve Your Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen Tickets](https://www.kkday.com/en-id/transportation/japan-rail/shinkansen/jp-tokyo-rail-to-jp-nagano-rail?cid=4624&ud1=tokyo-to-nagano&ud3=blog_97534) ## Cheapest Option: Tokyo to Nagano by Highway Bus If you’re traveling on a budget, the highway bus is the cheapest way to get from Tokyo to Nagano. ![A female traveler pulling a suitcase walks toward a pink and white Willer Express highway bus parked in a terminal](https://www.kkday.com/en/blog/wp-content/uploads/Tokyo-to-Nagano-by-Highway-Bus.webp)A traveler walking toward a Willer Express highway bus in Japan (via Japanese National Tourism Organization) While slower than the Shinkansen, it can cost less than half the price. # Tokyo to Nagano: 3 Ways to Travel in 2026 (Prices & Times)

![verified](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/image/icon/zx_icon1.png)Expert Reviewed By [Jerry](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/about-us/jerry.html)

Written by [Isaac](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/about-us/issac.html) \|Published: 2025-09-09\|Updated: 2026-08-28

How to get from [Tokyo](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/japan-tours/tokyo-tours/) to Nagano? You're looking at 220 kilometers northwest - about the same as New York to Boston, but with way better transport options.

Most people want to know the **fastest way** (Shinkansen, 90 minutes), the cheapest way (highway bus, ¥2,500), or if their JR Pass works (yes, on some trains).

Here's the deal: **Nagano**'s up in the mountains, home to snow monkeys, ancient temples, and some of [Japan's best skiing](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/japan-tours/ski-tours/). Whether you're coming from Tokyo city center or straight from the airport, you've got 3 main choices.

This **Tokyo to Nagano guide** breaks down exactly what you need to know - times, prices, and which option actually makes sense for your trip.

## Tokyo to Nagano Distance & 3 Options Comparison

Tokyo sits on Japan's eastern coast while Nagano is tucked into the mountains of central [Japan](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/japan-tours/), about **220 kilometers (137 miles)** northwest of the capital.

If you look at a map, you'll see Nagano right in the middle of Japan's main island, surrounded by the Japanese Alps. It's basically a straight shot northwest from Tokyo - think of it like going from New York City to the Catskill Mountains, but with better trains.

## Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen (Bullet Train) - Fastest Way to Travel

![Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/images/asia-tours/japan-tours/tokyo-nagano-shinkansen-700-3.jpg)

Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen

![Hokuriku Shinkansen](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/images/asia-tours/japan-tours/hokuriku-shinkansen-700-1.jpg)

Hokuriku Shinkansen

The Shinkansen is **Japan's high-speed rail system** \- those sleek, white trains with the long noses that whoosh past at 200+ mph.

For [Tokyo](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/japan-tours/tokyo-tours/) to Nagano, you'll ride the **Hokuriku Shinkansen line**. You'll depart from Tokyo Station (not Shinjuku or Shibuya - this catches some people out) and arrive at Nagano Station right in the city center. [Experience Japan at Bullet Train Speed >>](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/japan-tours/train-tours/)

Here's the thing about this route - there are three different train types, and picking the right one matters:

| **Train Type** | **Kagayaki** | **Hakutaka** | **Asama** |
| Travel Time | 1 hr 19 min | 1 hr 29 min | 1 hr 43 min |
| Stops | Only major stations | A few more stops | All stations |
| Price | ¥8,340 | ¥8,340 | ¥8,340 |
| JR Pass | No | Yes | Yes |
| Frequency | Every 1-2 hours | Every hour | Every hour |

**Kagayaki** is the speed demon - fastest but doesn't accept JR Pass.

**Hakutaka** makes a couple extra stops but takes JR Pass.

**Asama** is the local version, stopping everywhere but still pretty quick.

### Shinkansen Tokyo to Nagano Price

A regular reserved seat costs ¥8,340 one-way. That's about $55-60 depending on exchange rates.

- **Reserved seat (ordinary car):** ¥8,340 - This is what you want
- **Non-reserved seat:** ¥7,810 - Saves ¥530 but risky during busy times
- **Green Car (first class):** ¥11,410 - Bigger seats, quieter car
- **Gran Class:** ¥16,450 - Like business class on a plane (only on some trains)

### Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen Timetable

Trains run all day, roughly every 30-60 minutes. First train leaves [Tokyo](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/japan-tours/tokyo-tours/) at 6:16 AM, last direct train around 9:04 PM. After that, you'll need to transfer at Takasaki - annoying but doable.

Popular departure times from Tokyo:

- Early morning: 6:16, 6:52, 7:24
- Mid-morning: 8:24, 9:24, 10:24
- Afternoon: 12:24, 13:24, 14:24
- Evening: 17:00, 18:00, 19:00

The journey takes between **1 hour 19 minutes and 1 hour 43 minutes**, depending on whether you catch the faster Kagayaki or the Asama service that makes a few more stops.

### Shinkansen Tickets Tokyo to Nagano - How to Book & Save

![Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/images/asia-tours/japan-tours/tokyo-nagano-shinkansen-700-2.jpg)

Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen

![Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/images/asia-tours/japan-tours/tokyo-nagano-shinkansen-700-4.jpg)

Tokyo to Nagano Shinkansen

**Online** \- Book on JR East's website up to a month ahead. Gets you an e-ticket on your phone. Dead simple, plus you can pick your exact seat.

**At the station** \- Green ticket offices (みどりの窓口/Midori no Madoguchi) have English-speaking staff. Or brave the ticket machines - they have English mode. Tip: the machines near the Shinkansen gates are less crowded than the main ones.

**Convenience stores** \- Those ticket machines at 7-Eleven actually work for Shinkansen too. Interface is a bit clunky but it works.

**Travel agency** \- **Asia Odyssey Travel** can sort your tickets from our Tokyo office. We'll make sure you get the right train and explain everything in plain English.

If you're doing a round trip within a week, ask about the " **round trip discount**" \- saves about 10%. Planning multiple trips? The **JR East Nagano Niigata Pass** (¥18,000 for 5 days) pays for itself with just this round trip.

![Japan Bus](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/images/asia-tours/japan-tours/japan-bus-700-10.jpg)

Japan Bus

Willer Bus

Highway buses offer the **cheapest way to reach Nagano**. Choose the bus if you're on a tight budget or want to save on a night's accommodation with an overnight bus. However, remember that you'll arrive tired, which might affect your first day in Nagano.

Here's who runs buses on this route:

| **Bus Company** | **Price** | **Travel Time** | **Schedule** | **Notes** |
| Alpico (アルピコ) | ¥2,700-3,100 | 3.5 hours | 6:30 AM - 7:30 PM (8 daily) | Most frequent, reliable |
| Keio Bus | ¥2,500-3,500 | 3.5-4 hours | 7:00 AM - 11:30 PM | Night buses available |
| Willer Express | ¥2,000-4,000 | 4 hours | Various times | Prices vary wildly by date |
| JR Bus Kanto | ¥3,000-3,600 | 3.5 hours | 7:40 AM - 6:10 PM (5 daily) | Can use JR Pass (rare!) |

Go with **Alpico** \- they run this route most often and rarely cancel. Willer's super cheap seats sell out fast and their pricing is all over the place. JR Bus is solid but only useful if you've got a JR Pass that includes buses (most don't).

### Where to Catch Your Bus in Tokyo

**Shinjuku Highway Bus Terminal (Busta Shinjuku)** \- 4th floor of the building above Shinjuku Station South Exit. This is where most buses leave from. You're right at a major train hub.

**Tokyo Station Yaesu South Exit** \- Good if you're staying near Tokyo Station or coming from the east side of [Tokyo](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/japan-tours/tokyo-tours/). Fewer departures than Shinjuku though.

**Ikebukuro Station East Exit** \- Only a couple buses daily, but handy if you're staying in north Tokyo. Skip it otherwise.

**Shibuya Mark City** \- Limited service, mostly night buses. Only use if you're literally staying in Shibuya.

## Tokyo Airport to Nagano - Access from Narita & Haneda

![Tokyo to Nagano Bus](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/images/asia-tours/japan-tours/tokyo-nagano-bus-700-1.jpg)

Tokyo to Nagano Bus

![Tokyo to Nagano Bus](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/images/asia-tours/japan-tours/tokyo-nagano-bus-700-2.jpg)

Tokyo to Nagano Bus

Let's start with the regular routes. From either airport, you'll need to get to Tokyo Station first, then catch the Shinkansen to Nagano.

From Narita, take the Narita Express (60 minutes, ¥3,070), from Haneda, hop on the Tokyo Monorail (20 minutes, ¥500). Then it's the usual Shinkansen ride to Nagano.

But here's what you really want to know - during **ski season (mid-December through early March)**, there are direct buses to Hakuba, saving you the whole train shuffle.

Hakuba sits in a stunning valley below the Northern Japan Alps, about 40 kilometers west of Nagano city. This narrow valley - literally called "White Horse Valley" - packs in over 10 ski resorts, including Happo-One where they held the 1998 Winter Olympics.

It's 275 kilometers from [Tokyo](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/japan-tours/tokyo-tours/), but during winter, you can get there directly from both airports. [Ski Japan's Legendary Powder Snow >>](https://www.asiaodysseytravel.com/japan-tours/ski-tours/)

### From Narita Airport

Alpico runs one bus daily from **December 23 to March 9**. Heads out at 10:55 AM from Terminal 3, swings by T2 and T1 to grab more passengers.

Takes about 6 hours 10 minutes total. Heads up - they start this service pretty late in December, so early season skiers need to use the train route.

### From Haneda Airport

Same dates (December 23 - March 9), one bus daily leaving at 7:40 AM from Terminal 3. This one's faster at 5 hours 40 minutes since Haneda's closer to the mountains.

Both buses drop you at **Hakuba Happo Bus Terminal**. From there, catch the local shuttle buses that connect all the ski resorts, grab a taxi, or check if your hotel runs pickups. Most places in Hakuba offer some kind of shuttle service - just ask when you book.
